Hello from the FT newsroom, where we have been paying a lot of attention to a German state of just 2.1mn people. On Sunday Saxony-Anhalt catapulted the far-right party Alternative for Germany (AfD) to its best-ever election result, with 44 per cent of the vote. Ulrich Siegmund, whose inner circle includes at least two former members of neo-Nazi youth groups, could soon lead the most rightwing government to run a German state since the Third Reich. But what can the AfD’s victory in a small, relatively poor and elderly part of Germany’s former communist east tell us about the country writ large? Worryingly, quite a lot — as our reporters explain in this piece. Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who is about as popular as Keir Starmer was before he resigned as British prime minister, is running out of time to prove the political centre can still deliver. My choices this week US President Donald Trump wants to build a missile shield stretching from Earth into space in order to protect America from foreign missile attacks. But formidable engineering, financial and political obstacles stand in the way. This visual investigation uncovers the holes in Trump’s Golden Dome plan — and the companies cashing in on it. Our reporters reveal that Anthropic declined to submit its latest model to Britain’s AI Security Institute for testing before release. The decision has prompted fears inside the UK government that tech companies are falling into line with the Trump administration’s AI protectionism. (Free to read) For years Iran has imposed onerous hurdles on importers and exporters to control the supply of foreign currency. But according to Iranian businesses and regime insiders, Tehran has in recent months encouraged traders to repatriate funds by whatever means necessary — including via cryptocurrencies. What makes a great chief executive? Some will point to workforce sentiment, others to shareholder returns. But no single measure truly captures the role. Our new CEO Performance Ranking allows you to remix the data to find your own top-performing business leader from across the FTSE 100. Was Jesus anti-capitalist? If he were alive today, where would he sit on the political and economic spectrum? Find out on the latest episode of our video podcast series The Story of Money. Happy Thursday! *Bitcoin* is testing support around $77,000 after a hotter-than-expected *PPI* print, with *21Shares' Matt Mena* eyeing tomorrow's *CPI* data as the next catalyst for a move in either direction.

In today's newsletter, *Nasdaq* plans a $100 million investment in *Kraken's* parent company, *Brian Armstrong* says *bitcoin* has bottomed, researchers halve a *quantum* resource benchmark for attacking *Bitcoin* , and more.

Meanwhile, *Citadel Securities* urges ( https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-09-10-citadel-urges-sec-assert-oversight-event-contracts-tied-public-firms-414140?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) the *SEC* to assert oversight of event contracts tied to public firms.

*THE BIG ONE*

*💰 Nasdaq to invest $100 million in Kraken parent Payward as firms expand partnership*

( https://www.theblock.co/news/deals/2026-09-10-nasdaq-to-invest-100-million-in-kraken-parent-payward-as-firms-expand-partnership-414120?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

*Nasdaq's* venture arm agreed to invest $100 million in *Payward* , crypto exchange *Kraken's* parent company, deepening their partnership on tokenized equities and market infrastructure.

* The deal values Payward at $21 billion, per Bloomberg, and will see the firm adopt Nasdaq's market surveillance technology across its crypto, equities, tokenized equities, futures, and options venues.
* The firms are also targeting a second-quarter 2027 launch of *Nasdaq Equity Tokens* , or NETs, connecting them to Payward's *xStocks* ecosystem.
* Payward co-CEO *Arjun Sethi* said onchain settlement removes the wait from the U.S. clearing system, while keeping shareholder rights intact.
* Nasdaq President *Tal Cohen* said the investment reflects confidence that Payward can help build infrastructure to move capital while preserving trust and transparency.
